contentBlocks.body: A higher-order function takes a function as input or returns one. memoize(fn) does both: it returns a wrapper that remembers the result for each input it has seen. The cache lives in the closure, so it persists between calls but stays hidden from everyone else.

Memoizing is only safe for pure functions: the same input must always give the same output and cause no side effects. Memoizing a function that reads the clock or a database would return stale answers.
Use cache.has(n) rather than `if (cache.get(n))`. A cached result of 0, "" or false is falsy and would be recomputed every time.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Why must the cache be created inside memoize but outside the returned function?

choices: so it is created once per memoized function and survives between calls
so it is recreated on every call
because Map cannot be used inside arrow functions
so it becomes a global variable
payload.answer: so it is created once per memoized function and survives between calls
payload.explanation: If the Map were created inside the returned function, each call would start with an empty cache and nothing would ever be reused.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Which function is safe to memoize?

payload.explanation: Only a pure function always returns the same result for the same input. The others depend on time, randomness or external data.

payload.text: Only ____ functions are safe to memoize, because their output depends only on their input.
